sentences.text: Zephyrosaurus is a genus of orodromine ornithischian dinosaur known from a partial skull and postcranial fragments found in the Early Cretaceous Cloverly Formation of Montana.
This animal was approximately 1.8 meters long and weighed about 50 kilograms.
Some bones of Zephyrosaurus may have allowed for movement within the skull, known as cranial kinesis.
Zephyrosaurus possessed beak teeth, a trait shared with other orodromines.
The original description suggested Zephyrosaurus represented a previously unknown lineage of hypsilophodonts, similar in some respects to Hypsilophodon.
Fossil tracks from Maryland and Virginia have been attributed to Zephyrosaurus.
The type specimen MCZ 4392 consists of jaw fragments, the braincase, associated bones, partial vertebrae, and rib fragments.
Hans-Dieter Sues named the genus after finding it in the western United States, while C. R. Schaff was the one who found the specimen.
In 2003, Martha Kutter reported new remains of Zephyrosaurus at the Sam Noble Oklahoma Museum of Natural History, including bones from at least seven individuals covering all body regions.
Zephyrosaurus was a small, swift, bipedal herbivore.
Researchers suggest that Zephyrosaurus may have been capable of burrowing, similar to Orodromeus and Oryctodromeus.
Phylogenetic analysis in the 2010s classified Zephyrosaurus as a member of the Thescelosauridae family.
The fossil record of Zephyrosaurus spans from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
Some studies have struggled to classify Zephyrosaurus due to the fragmentary nature of the original fossil material.
